messages.msg: Lesson 05 fixes its sibling mistake by declaring readerName in App and writing it on two tags, <NewsHeader readerName={readerName} /> and <EditorialFeed readerName={readerName} />, read as props.readerName. The word props is New in Q05. Map 06 should recall that line as its starting point and explain the props object behind it, rather than introduce props as unseen.
messages.resolution: Map 06 recalls props from Q05 in Terms and the Prerequisite row for data-flows-down; props-are-arguments places the values on the parent's tags as Q05 did with props.readerName and explains the object behind it.

messages.msg: Q05 builds the Town News front page as a tree: App > NewsHeader, EditorialFeed > ArticleCard (> EditorialByline), MostRead. Its Real Mistake is ArticleCard reading const edition from inside App ('edition is not defined', page empty); the lesson fixes a fixed value with a top-level constant and says that a value belonging to the page travels down from the closest common parent, which Lecture 6 does with props. Map 06 can open on the same tree and pass edition down as a prop. Q05 also shows ArticleCard named twice printing the same story twice, which is Q06's hook.
messages.resolution: Map 06 builds its case study on Q05's tree: App writes edition={edition} on NewsHeader and EditorialFeed, which passes it on; Question 1's three identical cards are Q05's ArticleCard used three times (props-on-the-tag).

messages.msg: Message 05-06-01 described the archived map 05, which passed readerName as a prop. So props and the props object are New in Q06, not Recall from Q05; see 05-06-02 for the tree and the edition example to build on.
